doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Meeting in Buffalo and early careers
title: Jimmy's mentors from the service
summary: Jimmy had grown up around Jo Jones, Ben Webster, Lester Young and Chico Hamilton, who were in the service with him; Jeannie had stayed in Canada and the Midwest.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And I had just come back from California, not too long beforehand. And so that was kind of a habitual thing. After the gig was over and the pack up, and as Papa Jo Jones would say, “With our mutual armies we’ll move out smiling.”

But I was always hanging around because I liked the stories. See because he had more of an advantage in that he had a chance to grow up listening to people and talking to people like Jo Jones and Ben Webster—
And Lester Young and all these people, because they were in the service with him.
Yeah. Chico Hamilton and — I slept in the top bunk and Chico slept on the bottom you see?

And I hadn’t had that experience at all, because I stayed mostly up in Canada and in the middle part of the country where we played mostly. So I hadn’t had a chance to meet any of the big guys like that.
She played a lot for those big singers — all the top singers.
I know, but that was later. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
